# Rollout Plan: Migration of 40,000 Users from Legacy Billing to New Billing System

## Overview

This plan migrates 40,000 existing users from the legacy billing system to the new billing system while both systems run in parallel (dual-write/dual-run capable). Migration proceeds in named phases with explicit entry criteria, monitored metrics, and rollback capability at every stage. The legacy system remains fully operational as a fallback until well after the final user batch is confirmed stable.

---

## Phase 1: Canary (0.5% of users — ~200 users)

**Entry criterion:** New billing system has passed end-to-end integration testing in staging, including invoice generation, payment capture, refunds, proration, and tax calculation, with 100% parity against legacy outputs on a replayed sample of 10,000 historical transactions. Rollback tooling (single-command revert to legacy per account) is built and tested.

**Population:** Internal employee accounts and opted-in low-risk external users (monthly self-serve plans, no active disputes, no complex multi-entity billing).

**Duration:** 5 business days minimum, with at least 2 full billing cycles observed for any daily-billed accounts.

**Focus:** Validate data migration accuracy, dual-write consistency, and basic transaction flows under real (but low-blast-radius) traffic.

---

## Phase 2: Early Adopters (10% of users — ~4,000 users)

**Entry criterion:** Phase 1 completed with zero critical (Sev-1/Sev-2) billing defects open, error rate metric below halt threshold (see Metrics), and finance team has reconciled Phase 1 invoices against legacy-system shadow calculations with 100% match on a sampled audit of at least 500 transactions.

**Population:** A representative cross-section of plan types, geographies, and payment methods (cards, ACH, wallets), excluding enterprise/contract customers with custom billing terms.

**Duration:** 2 weeks, spanning at least one full monthly billing cycle for monthly-billed accounts.

**Focus:** Validate scale behavior, payment gateway load, dunning/retry logic, and support ticket volume/type.

---

## Phase 3: General Availability (40% of users — ~16,000 users)

**Entry criterion:** Phase 2 completed with no unresolved Sev-1/Sev-2 defects for 5 consecutive business days, support ticket volume attributable to migration below 1.5x the pre-migration baseline, and the CFO/finance controller has signed off on reconciliation accuracy for Phase 2 cohorts.

**Population:** Remaining self-serve and mid-market customers, batched by billing-cycle date to spread cutover load and avoid concentrating all invoicing events on a single day.

**Duration:** 3–4 weeks, migrating in weekly sub-batches (~4,000/week) to preserve the ability to halt mid-phase without having moved the whole cohort.

**Focus:** Full-scale performance validation, peak-load billing-run behavior, and continued reconciliation sampling.

---

## Phase 4: Final Migration — Enterprise & Complex Accounts (49.5% of users — ~19,800 users)

**Entry criterion:** Phase 3 completed with cumulative migrated-user error rate below halt threshold for the full phase duration, zero open Sev-1 defects, and a dedicated migration runbook reviewed with each enterprise account's assigned success manager (for accounts with custom contracts, multi-entity billing, or negotiated payment terms).

**Population:** Remaining enterprise, contract, and complex multi-entity accounts, migrated in small named batches with white-glove monitoring and pre-notified account owners.

**Duration:** 3–6 weeks depending on contract complexity; last batch requires explicit sign-off from account management before cutover.

**Note:** The legacy billing system is **not** decommissioned, disabled, or deleted as part of this phase or any prior phase. It remains live in read/fallback mode through a separate, subsequent **Decommission Phase**, gated on a minimum 60-day parallel-run stability window post-final-batch migration, a completed final financial reconciliation audit, and explicit sign-off from Finance, Engineering, and Legal/Compliance.

---

## Metrics and Halt Criteria

- **Billing error rate:** If the rate of failed, duplicated, or incorrect charges among migrated users exceeds **0.5% of transactions** in any rolling 24-hour window, halt the rollout immediately, freeze further migrations, and initiate root-cause analysis before resuming.
- Supporting (non-halting but tracked) signals: payment gateway latency p99, support ticket volume, reconciliation mismatch count, and dual-write divergence count between old and new systems.

---

## Risks

RISK: Payment data (card tokens, bank details) corrupted or mismatched during migration, causing failed charges | Run dual-write validation and automated reconciliation diffs before and after each batch; require zero-mismatch sign-off before advancing a phase | Data Migration Lead
RISK: New system miscalculates tax, proration, or currency conversion for edge-case billing configurations | Shadow-run new system against legacy for every invoice during Phases 1–3 and alert on any output divergence above a defined tolerance | Billing Engineering Lead
RISK: Customer-facing outage or double-billing incident damages trust and triggers support/chargeback spikes | Maintain instant per-account rollback to legacy system and pre-stage customer communications/credits for affected accounts | Customer Support & Trust Lead
RISK: Enterprise customers with custom contract terms are migrated incorrectly, causing invoicing disputes | Require account-manager sign-off and a dedicated test invoice cycle in staging before migrating any enterprise account | Enterprise Account Management Lead
RISK: Migration scripts fail silently, leaving a subset of users partially migrated in an inconsistent state | Implement idempotent migration jobs with post-migration state verification checks run automatically for every migrated account | Platform Reliability Engineer

---

PHASES: 4
